title: Delta-sync + resume strategy scratchpad
content:
Context / motivation:
- Working on a light-weight resume + delta sync story for long-running streamed responses and KV-cache checkpoints. Goal: minimize repeated tokens and allow client-side resume after network hiccups without replaying entire prompt/state.
- Primary consumers: mobile/edge SDKs, web clients that need reconnect, and private deployments where connection can be flaky.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Servers keep temporary ephemeral state for a bounded TTL (eg 10m) keyed by ResumeToken.
- We cannot rely on client clocks being synced.
- Resume tokens should be small, encryptable opaque strings (no PII).
- Need to support both: (A) purely stateless resume (server reconstructs from model checkpoint + small diff), and (B) stateful resume (server retains KV/cache and returns resume cursor).
- Latency-sensitive: initial reconnect path should be <200ms added overhead where possible.

High-level proposals (quick sketches):
1) Server-held ephemeral sessions + resume token (fastest):
   - When client starts a stream, server returns: Resume-Token, Cursor-Position, TTL. Server holds ephemeral state (KV cache, attention cache) for TTL (e.g., 10 min).
   - On reconnect, client calls /resume with Resume-Token + client-last-received-position. Server validates token, builds a diff (the missing tokens) and streams remaining tokens.
   - Pros: minimal recomputation, preserves performance. Cons: server memory, needs GC, multi-region routing complexity.

2) Checkpoint + delta (stateless friendly):
   - Server emits periodic checkpoints (compact snapshot ids) embedded in stream. Checkpoint includes: model-name, quantization-profile, kv-checksum, last-token-index, optional small delta blob (base64) with compressed state.
   - Resume: client POST /resume with last-checkpoint-id + last-token-index + minimal client context. Server reconstructs by loading model + checkpoint blob and continues generation.
   - Pros: scalable across regions, easier to persist. Cons: checkpoint size tradeoffs, slower resume (needs disk load), more complex snapshot protocol.

3) Hybrid: ephemeral state for hot sessions + checkpoint fallback
   - Keep ephemeral state for short TTL; also persist checkpoints every N tokens. On resume: try ephemeral token path first; fallback to checkpoint reconstruction if ephemeral expired.

API shape sketches (minimal, intentionally fuzzy):
- Start stream: POST /v1/generate-stream\  headers: Authorization, X-Client-Id\  body: {"model":"redwood-xxl","prompt":"...","resume_behavior":"ephemeral_or_checkpoint_prefer_ephemeral"}\  response: chunked stream, first meta-chunk: {"type":"session_init","resume_token":"<opaque>","cursor":0,"checkpoint_id":null,"ttl_seconds":600}

- Client reconnect (ephemeral): POST /v1/resume\  headers: Authorization, X-Client-Id, X-Resume-Token: <token>\  body: {"client_cursor": 234}  -> server responds with 200 chunked stream continuing tokens starting at 235.

- Client resume (checkpoint): POST /v1/resume-checkpoint\  body: {"checkpoint_id":"abc123","client_cursor":234,"client_context_hash":"h12"}\  response: server returns either 'ok-continue' with small warmup chunk OR 'reconstructing' + progress updates.

Resume token shape (opaque but spec):
- base64( AES-GCM( version||session_id||region||expiry||short-hash ) )
- server-side only: map session_id -> ephemeral state pointer + metrics. Keep version header to allow rotation.

Checkpoint format (textual sketch):
- checkpoint-id: sha256(modelname + kv-checksum + token_index + timestamp)
- payload: compressed proto with minimal kv entries (only last N layers keys), cache-policy bits, optionally an incremental replay log of last M tokens for append-only deterministic replay.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Resume token missing/expired: return 410 with suggestion: run a fresh request with prompt + client-suggested dedupe-hint field.
- Mismatch between client context and checkpoint (client sent different prompt): return 409 + recommended action (resend full prompt or server-side heuristic patch).
- Multi-region: token must include region or be globally resolvable; better to prefer global resume-as-reconstruct to avoid cross-region ephemeral lookups unless we replicate ephemeral state (expensive).

Backpressure + partial acks:
- Introduce "ack windows" where client sends X-ACK every N tokens; server can garbage-collect only after ack. Ack can be explicit HTTP POST with token + acknowledged-position, or implicit via websocket ping.
- Example: client sends {"ack_position": 1024, "resume_token":"tkn"} -> server advances last-ack, safe to drop oldest caches.

Security and privacy notes:
- Resume tokens are opaque; do not put raw prompt in token.
- If checkpoints contain customer data, they must be encrypted at rest using customer KMS where applicable (especially for private deployments).

Telemetry / observability:
- Emit metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_latency_ms, reconstruct_time_ms, ephemeral_hit_rate.
- Log minimal fingerprint instead of full prompt; keep sampling for debug with proper PII controls.

Edge / mobile considerations:
- Prefer smaller checkpoint frequency (bigger checkpoint size -> less server recompute). Mobile may have very short disconnects, so ephemeral TTL should be tuned per-client-class.
- In low-memory clients, store only last-checkpoint-id + last-token-index; server should handle most heavy lifting.

Example minimal JSON payloads (for clarity):
1) init response meta-chunk:
{
  "type": "session_init",
  "resume_token": "eyJ2ZXIiOiIxIiwi...",
  "cursor": 0,
  "checkpoint_id": null,
  "ttl_seconds": 600
}

2) client resume request (ephemeral):
POST /v1/resume headers: X-Resume-Token: tkn
body:
{
  "client_cursor": 235,
  "prefer_fast_resume": true
}

3) server error for stale token:
HTTP/1.1 410 Gone
{
  "error": "resume_token_expired",
  "recommendation": "restart_with_prompt_or_send_checkpoints"
}

Open questions / TODOs (quick list):
- TTL defaults by client-class (web vs mobile vs private) -> propose: web 2m, mobile 10m, private deployments configurable.
- Checkpoint frequency trigger: every N tokens OR size threshold OR semantic checkpoints (end-of-sentence). Tradeoff analysis needed.
- How much of attention/KV is necessary to persist for deterministic continuation? Could use probabilistic pruning to reduce checkpoint size. Need experiments.
- Multi-region ephemeral replication: do we replicate ephemeral state to 1 warm-follower region? cost analysis required.
- UX: what should client UI show when server returns 'reconstructing'? spinner + short message + estimated recon time.

Notes to self:
- Run quick benchmark: resume-latency (ephemeral) vs reconstruct-latency for 1GB checkpoint on NVMe vs hot-RAM.
- Talk to infra about ephemeral state eviction metrics and limits.
- Draft a short RFC if prototype results look promising.

Random ascii diagram (session lifecycle):
Client    -> Server: POST /generate-stream
  stream starts: server returns Resume-Token (ephemeral map)
  tokens flow -> client ACK windows -> server retains ephemeral state until TTL or acked
  disconnect -> client POST /resume with token -> server fast-path -> stream continues
  if token expired -> client POST /resume-checkpoint -> server reconstructs -> continue

End of scratchpad.

(Style: intentionally choppy; this is a personal design draft, not final spec. Keep on users/ for now.)
